# Discovery brief: Tutor matching

- **Status:** awaiting approval
- **Format:** 2
- **Profile:** Rapid; budget 30 minutes, used 27
- **Decision owner:** Founder, with the co-founder for D-3
- **Updated:** 2026-11-20 by discovery agent

## Resume here

- **Done:** Problem framed as a hypothesis; validate-first direction approved (D-2); investor claims settled (D-5); test scope and acceptance criteria drafted.
- **Waiting on:** Co-founder on the first segment (D-3); an answer on checks for tutors working with minors (Q-3) before the first lesson.
- **Next step:** Record the co-founder's answer on D-3, then ask the founder to approve the test scope and criteria (D-6).

## Problem

- **Request:** a tutoring marketplace with AI matching, in-app payments, video lessons and reviews for parents and adult learners, launching in three months (SRC-1).
- **Problem statement:** Parents of secondary school students in an exam year struggle to find a trusted, available tutor at short notice before exams, which leads to late or no help. It is solved when such parents get a suitable tutor proposal within two days and book again after the first lesson. This is a hypothesis (A-1).
- **Affected:** exam-year parents (looking for help); students; tutors (looking for steady clients). Adult learners have different needs and are out of this round (D-3).
- **Today:** unknown; presumed recommendations, notice boards and general tutoring sites (A-2). The only signal is interest in the concept (S-1), not evidence of a problem.
- **Why now:** the founders want to launch within three months (C-1) and are preparing an investor deck (S-4).

## Options and recommendation

| ID | Option | Value | Effort | Risk | Confidence | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| O-1 | Full marketplace as described, two segments. | H if demand exists | H | H | L | Months on an unproven problem; payments and minors add compliance work. |
| O-2 | Concierge test: one page and request form for one segment in one city; founders match by hand; parents pay tutors directly. | M | L | L | M | Tests demand and repeat use in four weeks, no code. |
| O-3 | Eight to ten structured parent interviews only. | L-M | L | L | M | Tests what people say, not what they do. |
| O-4 | List the founders' tutors on an existing tutoring site. | L | L | L | L | Tells little about the founders' own offer. |

**Recommendation (D-2, approved):** Validate first with O-2, alongside the interviews from O-3. The concept rests on friends' interest (S-1); four weeks of real requests and repeat bookings will show whether the problem exists before months go into O-1. Strong demand evidence from elsewhere (a waiting list, pre-payments) would change this.

## Scope

- **Must have:** a one-page description and request form for exam-year parents in one city, made with an existing site and form tool (R-1); a reply to every request within two days, including "no tutor available" (R-2); a log of each request and its outcome; a form that asks only what matching needs (R-3).
- **Non-goals:** None
- **Deferred:** the revenue model, until the test shows repeat bookings (D-4); adult learners, if D-3 is approved.

## Acceptance criteria


## Success

- **Outcome:** the founders know from behaviour, not opinion, whether exam-year parents need this enough to use it twice.
- **H-1:** We believe exam-year parents in one city will request a tutor through a simple matching service when exams approach. We will know when at least 15 requests arrive in four weeks and at least 40% of first lessons lead to a second booking. It is wrong if fewer than five requests arrive. The thresholds are the founder's targets, not benchmarks.
- **Impact estimate:** None. 10,000 users is the founder's target (S-4), labelled as such; the 30% outcomes claim is left out (D-5).
- **Could fail or backfire:** friends fill the form (track where each request came from); too few tutors turn it into a supply test (RK-1); a poor first tutor puts parents off (follow up after the first lesson).

| M-2 | Share of matched requests that lead to a first lesson | leading | unknown: counted in the test | none set; learn first |
| M-3 | Share of first lessons followed by a second booking within three weeks | lagging | unknown: counted in the test | target: 40% |
